intended_object: This is the canonical identification (A^S)^{G/S} ≅ A^G for an open normal subgroup S of G. In the library, A^G is encoded as `openSubgroupInvariants A ⊤`. I inferred this from the docstring and from the "Additive algebraic comparison" section of docs/FiniteTateTopology.md.
explanation:
The definition builds an R-linear equivalence between two Lean encodings of the same submodule. The first encoding is the G/S-invariants of the `quotientToInvariants` representation on A^S. The second is the library's `openSubgroupInvariants A ⊤`. Every component unwraps or rewraps nested subtypes: `x.1.1` in one direction, `⟨⟨x.1, _⟩, _⟩` in the other. The inverse laws and linearity all hold by `rfl`.

The docstring says as much: the map "forgets only redundant nested subtype data". The library uses it only as glue. It feeds the additive comparisons `finiteNormTargetAddEquivGroup` and `tateCohomology…AddEquivFiniteTate`, which match algebraic Tate cohomology with the library's compact-group constructions.

The underlying fact, that invariants under S and then under G/S are the G-invariants, is a real mathematical identity. As a definition, though, this declaration only transports elements between two representations of the same set. It is an implementation-level comparison isomorphism, not a mathematical object being defined. Read as that canonical isomorphism, it is correct: both maps send x to the same element of A.
